name: Daru Kothar (Gunpowder Magazine)
features: Later fireplace niche and smoke vent (non-original colonial alteration)
material: Deccan basalt ashlar masonry with lime mortar
source_document: Conservation and Repairs to Sinhagad Fort, Kimaya Architects (2017)
notes_and_uncertainties: Exact dimensions verified by measured survey drawing W-4. The fireplace niche was added in late 19th/early 20th century colonial use and must not be confused with original 18th-century gunpowder storage.

name: Pune Darwaza (Northern Citadel Gate)
features: Three successive defensive gateways ascending gorge
Tactical 90-degree right angle bend to negate war elephant battering rams
Flanking semicircular watch bastions with crenelated battlements
Pointed basalt archway (5.10m high x 3.20m wide)
material: Dressed hard basalt blocks with lime grouting
historical_period: Bahmani / Early Maratha era with 18th-century Peshwa reinforcements
source_document: Conservation and Repairs to Sinhagad Fort, Kimaya Architects (2017) & GIPE-194427
notes_and_uncertainties: Three distinct gateway thresholds verified in survey. Alignment strictly faces true North (~350° azimuth) overlooking the Pune approach.

name: Kalyan Darwaza (Southwest Gate)
features: Pointed basalt arch (4.80m height x 2.80m width)
Steep 32-degree stone stepped incline passage (18m length)
Direct pedestrian path descending towards Kalyan village and Torna Fort
source_document: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency (1885) & MTDC Survey
notes_and_uncertainties: Ground plan documented in archival maps. Controls southwestern mountain passes towards Torna and Rajgad.

name: Kalavantinicha Buruj (Courtesan's Bastion)
features: Protruding semicircular bastion over southern precipice
Modern 1.5m visitor safety parapet (2017 conservation addition)
material: Heavy dressed basalt masonry with dry-packed rubble core
source_document: Conservation and Repairs to Sinhagad Fort, Kimaya Architects (2017)
notes_and_uncertainties: Drawings S-5 to S-7 provide accurate surveyed profiles. Sits on high southern promontory overlooking Khadakwasla catchment.

name: Zunjar Buruj (Eastern Bulwark Bastion)
features: Long knife-edge eastern projecting defensive spur
Three heavy cannon embrasures commanding eastern approach to Purandar
Saffron Maratha Flag (Bhagwa Jhenda) mast at apex
Precipitous 250m sheer drops on both northern and southern flanks
material: Dressed hard black basalt ashlar and natural bedrock integration
source_document: Conservation and Repairs to Sinhagad Fort (2017) & Drone Survey 2026
notes_and_uncertainties: Verified in high-angle drone footage (frames 15-18). Acts as eastern visual and defensive anchor of the entire mountain.

name: Kandrai Buruj (Northwest Bastion)
material: Basalt coursed rubble with ashlar quoins
notes_and_uncertainties: Forms northern defensive arc connecting to Pune Darwaza.

name: Donagiricha Kada (Tanaji Kada / Dronagiri Cliff)
features: Site of the legendary 4 February 1670 night escalade led by Subedar Tanaji Malusare
Semicircular dressed stone bastion perched on cliff edge with stone stairway
material: Monolithic vertical basalt cliff with stone bastion crest
source_document: Sabhasad Bakhar, Gazetteer of Bombay Presidency & Drone Frame 14
notes_and_uncertainties: Drone footage frame 14 conclusively verifies the exact bastion and cliff morphology where the escalade was executed.

name: Barud Khana (Upper Munitions Vault)
material: Thick basalt masonry with lime mortar
notes_and_uncertainties: Secondary ordnance magazine situated in central upper sector.

name: Khankonda Tank Area
features: Four flanking wall bastions along perimeter curtain
Gun slits on outer defensive wall
material: Excavated bedrock with dressed basalt retaining walls
source_document: Conservation and Repairs to Sinhagad Fort, Kimaya Architects (2017)
notes_and_uncertainties: Four distinct wall bastions and gun slits verified in Drawing S-8.

name: Dev Taki (Sacred Sweet Water Cistern)
features: Pillar-supported monolithic rock chambers carved directly into mountain basalt
historical_period: Yadava / Early Koli Period (~11th - 13th Century CE)
notes_and_uncertainties: Natural underground springs maintain constant water level year-round even in peak summer.

name: Hathi Taki (Elephant Reservoir)
features: Originates as quarry for fortification wall basalt
Used for garrison cavalry horses, pack animals, and war elephants
material: Excavated bedrock basin with basalt stone retaining embankment
notes_and_uncertainties: Largest open water body on the fort plateau.

name: Ganga-Jamuna Taki (Twin Cisterns)
features: Separated by a living rock partition wall
Stone steps leading to water level
notes_and_uncertainties: Located on southern slope near Tanaji Samadhi.

name: Subedar Tanaji Malusare Memorial
features: Bronze bust and sword sculpture of Subedar Tanaji Malusare
Historic battle samadhi stone where Tanaji fell on 4 Feb 1670
Inscribed commemoration of 'Gad Aala Pan Sinh Gela'
material: Dressed stone plinth and bronze cast sculpture
historical_period: Modern commemoration on historic 1670 battle ground
notes_and_uncertainties: Marks the exact historic spot where Tanaji Malusare fell in victory during the night scaling of 1670.

name: Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj Samadhi
features: Carved stone pillars with floral Maratha motifs
Domed white chhatri roof with traditional kalash finial
material: Carved basalt stone with lime plaster
source_document: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Maharashtra & Drone Frame 07
notes_and_uncertainties: Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj passed away at Sinhagad on 3 March 1700. Drone frame 07 confirms exact octagonal chhatri form and terrace location.

name: Kaundinyeshwar Temple (Kondhaneshwar)
features: Ancient Shiva shrine from which Kondhana derives its name
Hemadpanthi style interlocking dry basalt stonework
Square garbhagriha (sanctum, 3.8m x 3.8m) with subterranean Shivling
Pillared Sabha Mandapa (6.5m x 6.5m) with carved basalt columns
material: Interlocking dressed basalt blocks without mortar
source_document: Bombay Gazetteer (1885) & Archaeological Records & Survey PDF 2
notes_and_uncertainties: Oldest verified continuous religious structure on the fort.

name: Lokmanya Tilak Bungalow
features: Pitched wooden roof truss with Mangalore tiles
Historic room where Lokmanya Tilak met Mahatma Gandhi in 1915
material: Stone, brick, seasoned timber, and red clay tiles
source_document: Pune Collectorate & Kesari Mahratta Trust Archives
notes_and_uncertainties: Maintained by the Kesari Mahratta Trust.
